_comment: Tenant-key membership matrix (#1189 / TRK-337), asserted on the shared key
It was the parity table of two hand-copies of one rule -- Go's
ValidateTenantKeys and Python's validate_tenant_keys. Neither judges key
names any more: whether a key is read is the shared verdict's (da-guard's
readings of the exporter), and a `version` label is the exporter's own
check (served-values' key_checks). Each case is one tenant key over a
verdict semantics: 'refuse' = what the tenant-api write gate refuses: the
verdict reads the key as unread (an error), or the exporter refuses its
`version` label; 'accept' = neither. A #1231 rename NOTICE is advisory and
Rows carrying "requires_alias": true spell the live deprecated alias
literally (mysql_cpu). They are only meaningful while that alias sits inside
its #1231 transition window, so the reader skips them when the alias table
is empty. Delete them when the window closes.

cases.name: flat key on the list is settable
cases.why: the point of the third slot

cases.name: flat key absent from both sets stays unknown
cases.why: the list is a membership set, not an amnesty

cases.name: prefix lookalike of a declared key stays unknown
cases.why: never prefix-match; the alias table forbids it for the same reason

cases.name: key in BOTH defaults and the list
cases.why: nothing enforces disjointness; a valued key stays valued

cases.name: _critical whose base is declared
cases.why: resolveCriticalRows keys off defaults[base]; the row would be dropped

cases.name: _critical whose base is valued
cases.why: unchanged pre-existing behaviour

cases.name: _critical key named ON the list
cases.why: 16 of the registry's 25 optional_overrides keys are this shape; Go's cascade never reaches membership for it

cases.name: _critical key AND its base both on the list
cases.why: still no base VALUE to emit against

cases.name: dimensional on a declared base
cases.why: resolveDimensionalRows is tenant-only and never consults defaults, so it emits

cases.name: dimensional on a valued base
cases.why: unchanged pre-existing behaviour

cases.name: dimensional spelling named ON the list
cases.why: the exporter serves a dimensional key from the tenant's value alone (resolveDimensionalRows), whatever the platform names, so the shared verdict reads it as read; the list neither adds nor takes anything here (ADR-038 §11; until then both hand-copies refused it on the parsed base)

cases.name: bad version label on a DECLARED base is still validated
cases.why: the base must be declared-and-not-valued so this actually exercises the new dimensional branch; ADR-024 OQ-6 validation has to run there too, or the branch becomes a way to smuggle version labels past the guard

cases.name: bad version label on a valued base
cases.why: unchanged pre-existing behaviour, kept as the control for the row above

cases.name: reserved key is unaffected by the list
cases.why: reserved keys short-circuit before membership on both sides

cases.name: reserved prefix is unaffected by the list
cases.why: as above

cases.name: typo'd reserved key is not rescued by the list
cases.why: the typo signal must survive

cases.name: list carries the RETIRED spelling, tenant uses the canonical one
cases.why: the list must be canonicalized by the same table, or it declares a permanently un-settable key

cases.name: list carries the canonical spelling, tenant uses the retired one
cases.why: the rename transition window applies to declared keys too (advisory NOTICE only)

cases.name: retired _critical spelling on the list, canonical _critical written
cases.why: canonicalizes to the _critical shape, which is refused regardless of spelling

cases.name: duplicate list entries collapse
cases.why: membership is a set on both sides

cases.name: both spellings of one threshold on the list collapse
cases.why: canonicalization makes them one member

cases.name: whitespace-padded list entry does NOT match
cases.why: neither side strips. Recorded as a KNOWN SHARED GAP, not an endorsement: silently trimming would normalise a malformed platform file the way the rejected lowercase-coercion would have. The fix belongs in list-content validation, and this row exists so that fix has to update one table instead of hunting two suites.

cases.name: empty list entry matches nothing
cases.why: same shared gap as the row above
